pages.title: Cardiology consultation (dictated)
lines: Mr. Delacroix is a sixty-seven-year-old gentleman, seen today at the request of Dr. Haugen for consideration of a defibrillator. He had an inferolateral myocardial infarction in March of 2020 treated with a stent to the circumflex. He has not had any further cardiac events or procedures since that time.
His echocardiogram from earlier this month shows an ejection fraction of twenty-seven percent, which is not much different from last year.

Functionally, he tells me he gets short of breath after one flight of stairs and has to pause when walking his dog more than a block or so. He has occasional exertional chest tightness, Canadian Cardiovascular Society class II, relieved by rest. No rest symptoms. No syncope.
IMPRESSION: Ischemic cardiomyopathy, ACC/AHA stage C heart failure with reduced ejection fraction. Stable angina CCS class II. He has been on guideline-directed therapy for several years.
RECOMMENDATION: Primary prevention ICD is reasonable. He will meet with our nurse practitioner for a formal shared decision-making visit.
Dictated by Siobhan Mercer-Aho, MD. D: 09/17/2026 T: 09/18/2026

nyha_class.why: No NYHA class appears anywhere. 'ACC/AHA stage C' is a heart failure stage, not a NYHA class. 'CCS class II' is an angina scale. A symptom description and a 6-minute walk distance are not a documented NYHA class.
